definitions.explanation: The remains or site of a former castle. Japan has hundreds of castle ruins, many of which are popular tourist destinations and historical landmarks.

examples.japanese: {城跡|しろあと}を{見学|けんがく}した。
この{城跡|しろあと}は{桜|さくら}の{名所|めいしょ}としても{知|し}られている。
examples.english: This castle site is also known as a famous spot for cherry blossoms.

examples.japanese: {石垣|いしがき}だけが{残|のこ}る{城跡|しろあと}からは、{町|まち}が{一望|いちぼう}できる。
examples.english: From the castle ruins where only the stone walls remain, you can see the whole town.

notes:
USAGE:
{城跡|しろあと} refers to the site where a castle once stood, including any remaining structures like stone walls or moats. Many Japanese {城跡|しろあと} are designated as historical sites.

PRONUNCIATION:
Also read as じょうせき in more formal or academic contexts, but しろあと is the standard everyday reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {城跡|しろあと}を{訪|たず}ねる: to visit castle ruins
- {城跡|しろあと}{公園|こうえん}: castle ruins park
- {城跡|しろあと}の{石垣|いしがき}: stone walls of castle ruins

FORMS:
{城|しろ} (castle) + {跡|あと} (remains, trace).
